source.title: Norm-based Generalization Bounds for Compositionally Sparse Neural Networks
source.authors: Tomer Galanti; Mengjia Xu; Liane Galanti; T. Poggio

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the full paper and appendices; no file problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically measures a norm-based bound alongside the train–test generalization gap, testing whether a measured network property tracks that gap. It does not test the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measured norm-based bounds and train/test errors on natural-label classification tasks. Its discussion of random labels and other cited studies is background, not an experiment on memorizing random labels. The norm-based measure is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study derives sparsity-aware norm bounds and evaluates a norm-based quantity against generalization gaps. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness (V7), compare convolutional with fully connected classifiers (V3), or test any other listed version. Related theoretical arguments about sparsity do not establish the comparative performance V3 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive improved norm-based bounds for sparse networks without requiring weight sharing, describe their empirical estimates as relatively tight on simple classification tasks, and suggest sparsity is important to architectural success. They explicitly acknowledge that their bounds are not practical in general; they do not experimentally establish CNN superiority over fully connected networks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives a different norm-based bound and evaluates its relationship to the generalization gap; it does not reproduce any listed intervention or measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set size changes the measured gap and bound. Appendix experiments describe depth and channel-count comparisons, but provide figure-based results without extractable numeric values.

fits_no_version.finding: On binary CIFAR-5m classification, generalization gaps generally decrease with sample size while the measured norm remains bounded. The authors describe rho(w)/sqrt(m) as relatively tight, although this quantity substantially exceeds the reported gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these CNNs trained with MSE, weight normalization and weight decay, a sparsity-aware norm quantity decreases with sample size alongside the generalization gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical bounds incorporate sparse connectivity without requiring weight sharing. Appendix experiments report smaller gaps with greater depth and qualitative bound–gap tracking during training on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-network norm bounds can exploit architectural connectivity, and their empirical relationship with generalization depends on architecture and training conditions.

record.problems: Experiments use simple classification problems; test error is estimated from 1000 test samples per class. The tables report averages over 5 runs without uncertainty estimates. The claimed tightness is described, but the study does not report a statistical test of correlation.
record.rows_left_out: No tabled measured results were omitted. Appendix Figures 3–5 report depth and channel variations as plots; the text describes qualitative trends but does not provide recoverable numeric values for individual settings.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe; random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold. Appendix channel sweeps do not establish this threshold or continued test-error reduction.
Comparative test error of convolutional and fully connected networks, learned locality, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout across dataset sizes and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The row values agree with the tables. Their states cannot express evidence for a listed version because all version links are none. The measured rho(w)/sqrt(m) is a scaling term, not the complete numerical bound in Theorem 3.2. Its values and the generalization gaps alone do not test V7. No omitted result bearing on V1–V8 was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels are not experimentally compared.
No one-hidden-layer width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks for test error.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.

The experiments measure a product-of-layer-norms generalization bound, not magnitude-aware sharpness under weight perturbations, and do not compare it with norm- or margin-based measures as V7 specifies.
